knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The fault is in how the liner sits and fits the bin. Refitting and checking the size is the fix. Pushing the liner down hides sharp items.
Spare liners in the base let the next change happen without stopping the route.
Torn, wet, leaking or food-soiled liners are replaced at once. Waiting for a full bin is not the rule.

practicalCriteria: Checks the liner size against the site card before fitting it to a bin.
Seats the liner flat over the rim, ties it snugly, and confirms the lid closes.
Replaces a torn, wet or food-soiled liner during the route and does not press waste down by hand.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80% pass mark, which for three questions means all three correct. Practical sign-off is separate and observed by an assessor.
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation of liner changes on a route
Site card entries for any size problems
stopWorkCriteria: Waste pressed down by hand or foot inside a bin
Liner left in a bin after it has become wet or torn
